headline_insight: While the 2026 Insurance Survey reveals an overall positive Net Promoter Score of 16.8 across 2,104 clients, significant gender-based disparities exist in product uptake, with male clients heavily concentrated in Health Insurance while female clients show higher relative participation in Enhanced Credit Life and Crop Insurance.
paragraphs: The 2026 VisionFund Insurance Survey captured responses from a total of 2,104 clients, yielding an overall Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 16.8. This score is comprised of 43.9% promoters, 28.9% passives, and 27.1% detractors, indicating a generally positive reception but highlighting a substantial segment of dissatisfied clients. Benchmark data is not available for this indicator to compare these results against wider industry standards, and qualitative client voice quotes were not collected for this demographic overview. For VisionFund's programming, the presence of 27.1% detractors signals an urgent need to conduct deep-dive qualitative assessments to identify the pain points driving client dissatisfaction, ensuring that future product iterations address these underlying issues to improve retention and social impact.

Geographically, the survey's reach is highly concentrated in African nations, with Ghana and Zambia representing the largest female client cohorts at 16.6% (252 clients) and 14.2% (216 clients) of the female sample respectively, while Uganda and Rwanda represent the largest male cohorts at 19.6% (115 clients) and 17.6% (103 clients). Conversely, the representation of Latin American countries is extremely limited, with Mexico having only four female clients and one male client, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Honduras each having only one female client, and the Dominican Republic having only one male client. Because these Latin American subgroups have extremely small sample sizes, these specific regional findings must be treated as directional and illustrative rather than statistically robust. Since benchmark data and verbatim client quotes are not available for these country-level indicators, VisionFund's product design teams must focus resources on the robust African datasets while expanding future survey efforts in Latin America to gather statistically viable insights before launching targeted regional campaigns.

Analysis of insurance product types reveals clear gender-based segmentation, particularly within Health Insurance, which is held by 90.8% of male clients (532) compared to 75.1% of female clients (1,140)—a notable difference of -15.7 percentage points. In contrast, female clients exhibit higher relative participation in Enhanced Credit Life at 16.6% (252 clients) compared to 5.6% of males (33 clients), as well as Crop Insurance at 8.3% (126 clients) compared to 3.6% of males (21 clients). Benchmark data and qualitative client voices are not available for these product indicators. The programming implication of this divergence is that VisionFund must design gender-responsive marketing and enrollment strategies to bridge the health insurance gap for women, while simultaneously leveraging the stronger female footprint in credit-linked and agricultural insurance to bundle value-added services that support women's economic empowerment and agricultural resilience.
